blocks.text: 1. Teacher Forcing
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785445739353-101078575.png

Sequence-to-Sequence Learning, the previous topic, introduced a decoder generating output one time step at a time. Teacher Forcing is a training technique used when generating sequential output, explored throughout this topic.

It works by feeding the genuinely correct previous word during training, rather than the model's own, possibly wrong, prediction, a genuinely important training detail covered throughout the rest of this topic.
2. Recapping The Decoder's Own Structure

This connects back to the decoder starting from context, already covered in Sequence-to-Sequence Learning. The decoder genuinely generates output one time step at a time, each step conditioned on prior words.
A genuinely important training question follows: which prior words should feed into the next step during training, a genuinely real decision explored throughout the rest of this topic.
3. The Training Choice
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785445739353-579003486.png
A genuinely important training decision arises here. Option one feeds the model's own genuinely predicted previous word back in, using whatever the network itself just generated.
Option two feeds the genuinely correct, true previous word from the training data instead, a genuinely different choice explored in complete detail throughout the rest of this topic.

blocks.text: 4. Teacher Forcing, Defined
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785445739353-891971280.png

This connects back to option two, already covered in this topic. Teacher Forcing genuinely chooses that second option: feed the genuinely correct, true previous word, rather than the model's own prediction.

This happens regardless of what the model itself may have predicted at that step, giving this technique its own distinctive, descriptive name: a "teacher" genuinely forcing the correct answer at every step.
5. Why This Genuinely Speeds Up Training

blocks.alt: Why This Genuinely Speeds Up Training
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785445739353-957310381.png
This connects back to Training Loops, already covered in the Training Deep Networks module. Errors compounding across time steps are a genuinely real risk without Teacher Forcing.

Teacher Forcing genuinely prevents one early, wrong prediction from throwing off every subsequent step during training, keeping training genuinely stable and efficient rather than letting mistakes cascade.

blocks.title: info
blocks.content: Without Teacher Forcing, already covered in this topic, a single early mistake could genuinely derail an entire training sequence, making it far harder for the network to learn correctly from later, otherwise valid time steps.

blocks.text: 6. The Exposure Bias Problem
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785445739353-359525478.png

A genuinely honest, real limitation connects back to inference, already covered as distinct from training throughout this course. At inference time, the genuinely true previous word is not actually available, only the model's own prediction is.
This creates a genuinely real, honest mismatch between how the model trains and how it actually gets used, a genuinely important limitation explored further in the very next section.
7. The Training-Inference Gap

This connects back to Training Loops and Validation Loops, both already covered in the Training Deep Networks module. Training genuinely sees correct prior words; inference genuinely only sees its own, possibly wrong, prior predictions.
This is called exposure bias, a genuinely real, honest gap between training and inference conditions, directly resulting from the training choice already covered earlier in this topic.

blocks.text: 8. A Preview Of Scheduled Sampling
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785445740359-961632058.png

A genuinely practical, real mitigation connects back to the exposure bias problem, already covered in this topic. Scheduled sampling genuinely mixes in some of the model's own predictions during training too.

This genuinely gradual approach helps narrow the training-inference gap already covered in the previous section, exposing the model to some of the same conditions it will genuinely face at inference time.
9. Recognizing When Teacher Forcing Is Genuinely Valuable

blocks.alt: Recognizing When Teacher Forcing Is Genuinely Valuable
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785445740360-247312377.png

This connects back to training Sequence-to-Sequence models, already covered in the previous topic. Teacher Forcing, already covered in this topic, directly speeds up and stabilizes that training process.
This connects back to the exposure bias tradeoff, already covered in this topic. Being genuinely aware of the training-inference gap, already covered, matters when deploying such a model.
10. Worked Example

The example below directly demonstrates the contrast between training with Teacher Forcing versus without it, showing how an early mistake can genuinely cascade without this technique, illustrating the concepts already covered throughout this topic.

code.content:
true_sequence = ["le", "chat", "etait", "assis"]

def predict_next_word(previous_word, rng):
    # a genuinely simplified, sometimes-wrong stand-in decoder
    word_map = {"le": "chat", "chat": "etait", "etait": "assis", "assis": "END"}
    if rng.random() < 0.3:  # a genuinely simulated mistake, 30% of the time
        return "WRONG_WORD"
    return word_map.get(previous_word, "END")

import numpy as np
rng = np.random.RandomState(7)

print("With Teacher Forcing (already covered in this topic, always using the true previous word):")
for t in range(1, len(true_sequence)):
    predicted = predict_next_word(true_sequence[t - 1], rng)  # genuinely always uses the true previous word
    print(f"  Time step {t}: true previous word '{true_sequence[t - 1]}' -> predicted '{predicted}'")

print("\nWithout Teacher Forcing (already covered as exposure bias in this topic, using the model's own prior prediction):")
previous_prediction = true_sequence[0]
for t in range(1, len(true_sequence)):
    predicted = predict_next_word(previous_prediction, rng)  # genuinely uses its own, possibly wrong, prior prediction
    print(f"  Time step {t}: fed previous prediction '{previous_prediction}' -> predicted '{predicted}'")
    previous_prediction = predicted  # a genuinely wrong prediction here would cascade forward

blocks.title: info
blocks.content: Running this example shows the "without Teacher Forcing" path potentially cascading a single wrong prediction into every subsequent step, exactly the risk already covered in this topic as the motivation for using Teacher Forcing during training.

blocks.text: 11. Key Takeaways

items: Teacher Forcing feeds the correct previous word during training, not the model's own prediction.
This addresses which prior word should condition each decoder time step during training.
It prevents one early, wrong prediction from cascading through every subsequent training step.
At inference time, the true previous word is not actually available, only the model's own prediction.
This training-inference mismatch is called exposure bias.
Scheduled sampling gradually mixes in the model's own predictions during training to reduce this gap.
Teacher Forcing directly speeds up and stabilizes Sequence-to-Sequence model training.
